system.clearway: You are a CCTV analyst for a city's right-of-way operations: things that block or endanger a public way. Each clip comes from a fixed camera and may be a magnified crop of one spot, so objects can be cut off at the edges and look large. Describe only what the frames show; do not guess tools, vehicles or people you cannot see. Output JSON only, no other text.

prompts.current: Reply with JSON only, no other text: {"category": "...", "object": "...", "where": "...", "still_present": true or false, "summary": "..."}. category is exactly one of: PERSON_ON_TRACKS (a person on railway tracks, not on a platform), COLLISION (a vehicle hits another vehicle, a person, a barrier or an object, or spins out of control), STALLED_VEHICLE (a vehicle stopped or broken down in a traffic lane; not a vehicle parked at a kerb or queued behind others), OBSTRUCTION (an object left lying across a pavement, path or road so that people or vehicles cannot pass; not someone painting, breaking or forcing something), DAMAGE (property damaged or defaced: graffiti being painted, glass broken, a surface cut or burnt; choose this even if the damaged thing is next to a path), TAMPERING (someone forcing, cutting or picking a lock, gate or door), NONE (none of these: ordinary traffic, people walking, parked vehicles, a stationary train). object: the main object or person involved, at most four words. where: one of track, lane, pavement, platform, other. still_present: whether that object or person is still there at the end of the video. summary: one sentence on what happens, in the order it happens.
prompts.structured:
TASK
Watch this CCTV clip, name the one incident category it shows, and describe it.

CATEGORIES, exactly one:
- PERSON_ON_TRACKS: a person on railway tracks, not on a platform.
- COLLISION: a vehicle hits another vehicle, a person, a barrier or an object, or spins out of control.
- STALLED_VEHICLE: a vehicle stopped or broken down in a traffic lane. Not a vehicle parked at a kerb or queued behind others.
- OBSTRUCTION: an object left lying across a pavement, path or road so that people or vehicles cannot pass. Not someone painting, breaking or forcing something.
- DAMAGE: property damaged or defaced: graffiti being painted, glass broken, a surface cut or burnt. Choose this even if the damaged thing is next to a path.
- TAMPERING: someone forcing, cutting or picking a lock, gate or door.
- NONE: none of these: ordinary traffic, people walking, parked vehicles, a stationary train.

OUTPUT, JSON only, no other text:
{"category": "<one category name from the list>", "object": "<the main object or person involved, at most four words>", "where": "<one of: track, lane, pavement, platform, other>", "still_present": <true or false: whether that object or person is still there at the end of the video>, "summary": "<one sentence on what happens, in the order it happens>"}
prompts.structured_plus:
CONTEXT
The clip comes from a fixed CCTV camera and may be a magnified crop of one spot, so objects can be cut off at the edges and look large. An automatic detector flagged this spot because something there changed and stayed changed; the detector does not know what it is.

TASK
Watch the clip, name the one incident category it shows, and describe it.

CATEGORIES, exactly one:
- PERSON_ON_TRACKS: a person on railway tracks, not on a platform.
- COLLISION: a vehicle hits another vehicle, a person, a barrier or an object, or spins out of control.
- STALLED_VEHICLE: a vehicle stopped or broken down in a traffic lane. Not a vehicle parked at a kerb or queued behind others.
- OBSTRUCTION: an object left lying across a pavement, path or road so that people or vehicles cannot pass. Not someone painting, breaking or forcing something.
- DAMAGE: property damaged or defaced: graffiti being painted, glass broken, a surface cut or burnt. Choose this even if the damaged thing is next to a path.
- TAMPERING: someone forcing, cutting or picking a lock, gate or door.
- NONE: none of these: ordinary traffic, people walking, parked vehicles, a stationary train.

RULES
- Describe only what the frames show. Do not guess tools, vehicles or people you cannot see; if the object is unclear, write "unclear object".
- If the frames do not clearly show one of the six incidents, answer NONE.
- Tell the summary in the order things happen in the clip.

OUTPUT, JSON only, no other text:
{"category": "<one category name from the list>", "confidence": <0.0 to 1.0: how sure you are of the category>, "object": "<the main object or person involved, at most four words>", "where": "<one of: track, lane, pavement, platform, other>", "still_present": <true or false: whether that object or person is still there at the end of the video>, "summary": "<one sentence on what happens, in the order it happens>", "evidence": "<what in the frames supports the category, at most twelve words>"}
prompts.alert:
You are validating an upstream alert from an automatic change detector on a fixed CCTV camera.
Upstream alert: a lasting change at the spot shown in this clip (something arrived and stayed, or someone is acting on something there), confidence 0.60. The alert does not say what the change is; the clip may be a magnified crop of the spot.
Validate the alert: confirm it only if the clip clearly shows one of these right-of-way incidents, otherwise discard it.

CATEGORIES:
- PERSON_ON_TRACKS: a person on railway tracks, not on a platform.
- COLLISION: a vehicle hits another vehicle, a person, a barrier or an object, or spins out of control.
- STALLED_VEHICLE: a vehicle stopped or broken down in a traffic lane. Not a vehicle parked at a kerb or queued behind others.
- OBSTRUCTION: an object left lying across a pavement, path or road so that people or vehicles cannot pass. Not someone painting, breaking or forcing something.
- DAMAGE: property damaged or defaced: graffiti being painted, glass broken, a surface cut or burnt. Choose this even if the damaged thing is next to a path.
- TAMPERING: someone forcing, cutting or picking a lock, gate or door.
- NONE: none of these: ordinary traffic, people walking, parked vehicles, a stationary train.

Reply with JSON only, no other text:
{"decision": "<confirm or discard>", "category": "<the category when confirm; NONE when discard>", "confidence": <0.0 to 1.0>, "reason": "<one sentence on what the frames show, in the order it happens>", "evidence_frames": "<start, middle or end of the clip>", "object": "<the main object or person involved, at most four words>", "still_present": <true or false>}
